stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML topics including 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The model is associated with Meta (formerly Facebook) and uses the 'safetensors' format.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and features native DFlash and image input support via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: Sony Music and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Major music rights holders (Sony Music and Warner Chappell) are suing AI company Anthropic.
The lawsuit alleges unauthorized use of 'tens of thousands' of copyrighted musical works.
The financial stakes are high, with potential damages reaching $150,000 per work.

stories.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
stories.author: Ola Shorinwa
bullet_points: Introduces CLAP, a new framework for cross-embodiment action-conditioned video generation.
Addresses the limitation of current models being restricted to a single robot embodiment, hindering generalizable physics learning.
Allows training on diverse, internet-scale videos featuring both human and robotic agents to learn universal physical laws.

stories.title: Token-Level Advertising
stories.author: Qi Qi
bullet_points: Proposes Latent Advertiser Mixture Auction (LAMA) to revolutionize advertising in generative AI.
Moves beyond traditional slot-based advertising by embedding advertiser influence directly into the token generation process.
Advertisers influence next-token policies by reporting local continuation values, which the platform then decodes.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to key ML technologies like transformers and Llama.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30-billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks requiring context gathering and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) utilizing the MLX framework.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster specifically when integrated with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM deployment.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads for macOS users.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: Google further buries search results under AI mode
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google is automatically expanding its AI search summaries (AI Overviews) on the search results page.
This expansion pushes traditional organic search links significantly further down the results page.
The change represents an ongoing shift in how Google integrates generative AI into its core search functionality.

stories.title: Trump blacklisting of "woke" Anthropic deemed illegal by federal judge
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A federal judge ruled that a purported blacklisting of Anthropic by Trump was illegal.
Anthropic has publicly opposed the use of its technology in lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance.
The ruling highlights legal challenges surrounding government actions targeting AI companies.

stories.title: Authorities arrest 2 alleged members of prolific hacking group TeamPCP
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Authorities have arrested two alleged members of the hacking group TeamPCP.
TeamPCP conducted a large-scale, relentless supply-chain attack campaign.
The group successfully infected over 1,000 organizations.

stories.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
stories.author: Haoliang Li
bullet_points: Introduces RedEvoAgent, an automatic red-teaming agent designed to evolve its skills based on experience.
Highlights the increased risk associated with LLM agents executing tools, where jailbreaks can lead to harmful state changes beyond simple text generation.
Addresses limitations in current red-teaming methods, specifically the reliance on fixed attacks and the bias issues in trajectory-based retrieval.

stories.title: CorporateBench: Large-Scale Q&A Benchmarking with Temporal Knowledge Bases
stories.author: Igor Labutov
bullet_points: Introduces CorporateBench (CB), a large-scale, human-validated Q&A benchmark designed for enterprise-scale document collections.
Addresses the critical evaluation challenge in LLMs by providing a realistic benchmark that avoids the privacy issues of internal corporate data.
Evaluates LLMs across multiple tasks using a massive corpus exceeding 230,000 documents, focusing on complex, real-world corporate communication scenarios.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run and utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary LLM interfaces and local, open-source model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Sophistication of generative audio tools is leading to widespread AI-generated music.
The rise of AI music raises intellectual property concerns regarding algorithmic derivation from human artists' work.
There is a growing issue of attribution, with some creators openly using AI and others denying its use.

stories.title: Xbox CEO calls Project Helix a ‘family of devices’
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma clarified that 'Project Helix' is not a single console.
Helix is being redefined as a 'family of devices' for the next generation of Xbox.
This shift suggests a broader ecosystem approach rather than a singular hardware release.

stories.title: I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.
stories.author: Reece Rodgers, wired.com
bullet_points: Privacy requests sent to 100 companies often resulted in confusion.
Many companies failed to properly handle or respond to data deletion requests.
The study highlights significant friction and lack of clarity in current data privacy practices.

stories.title: Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta has implemented a safety feature update for its AI glasses.
The update prevents the glasses from recording when the user covers the safety light.
This change addresses privacy concerns related to nonconsensual recording capabilities.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile and persist specialized knowledge and workflows learned by AI agents.
It addresses the limitation where valuable insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and reuse learned skills across multiple interaction iterations.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM software debugging by noting that successful agent trajectories may still contain suboptimal steps.
The paper introduces 'SWE-Prime' as a method to improve LLM performance on real-world software issues by addressing noisy supervision.
It suggests moving beyond simple Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on raw successful trajectories to mitigate the risk of models imitating undesirable behaviors.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Current LLM-based code review models often treat the process as a single, static decision.
Real-world code review is inherently iterative and interactive, involving multi-round dialogue.
The paper introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark LLMs against the complex, dynamic nature of actual code review.

stories.title: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
stories.author: Philippe Schwaller
bullet_points: Introduces MAELLE, a new method for predicting chemical reactions using discrete flow matching.
The approach models reactions not as molecular topology edits, but as transformations in electron occupation vectors.
This represents a shift from traditional generative or heuristic ML models in computational chemistry.

stories.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
stories.author: Yisen Xi
bullet_points: Introduces Persona-Execution Separation (PES) as an architectural pattern for LLM agents.
Addresses the conflict between allowing LLM personas to evolve freely and maintaining traceable, audited execution.
Achieves separation by placing persona and execution in distinct trust domains connected by a governed contract bridge.

stories.title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners
stories.author: Indranil Sanyal
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in current AI security scanner evaluation, which often only measure successful judgments.
The study benchmarks three existing scanners (ModelScan, ModelAudit, Fickling) using a controlled, artifact-backed synthetic corpus.
The evaluation covers 170 Pickle and PyTorch artifacts across 145 specimen families, including those with known security vulnerabilities.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: Research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) internally structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs differentiate between specific Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models to map these moral concepts geometrically.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: Addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed-weight sepsis severity indices in modern critical care.
Presents a two-site retrospective study involving over 36,000 adult patients to develop a new continuous severity score.
The core innovation is developing a sepsis score learned directly from patient trajectories without requiring hour-by-hour supervision.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge beyond simple content detection.
The study employs six independent linear probes, mapping to the six categories of Moral Foundations Theory (MFT).
The core aim is to determine if LLMs organize these moral foundations geometrically and distinguish between them.

stories.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
stories.author: Wenguang Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost barrier in language model pretraining, a major hurdle for open-source and academic research.
Presents 'Puro-2B,' a model trained using a single, consumer-grade RTX 5090, demonstrating cost-efficiency.
Contributes to the growing trend of accessible, open-source training recipes for large language models (LLMs).

stories.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO
stories.author: Zhenkun Wang
bullet_points: The paper investigates Evolution Strategies (ES) as a memory-efficient post-training method for improving LLM reasoning.
It addresses the lack of understanding regarding ES optimization behavior compared to established methods like GRPO.
The research empirically and theoretically demonstrates that ES offers a performance advantage over GRPO in LLM reasoning tasks.

stories.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
stories.author: Ting Zhu
bullet_points: Introduces CritICL, a novel inference-time framework designed to enhance LLM reasoning.
Addresses the inefficiency of current methods (like repeated generation) used to improve LLM performance.
Leverages the insight that LLM failure modes follow structured patterns across different model scales within the same family.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experience into reusable skills.
The system addresses the limitation of scattered insights by creating persistent knowledge structures for skill development.
This enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities through continuous interaction and knowledge reuse.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of using only successful agent trajectories for training LLMs to solve software issues.
The core problem identified is that successful trajectories can still contain ineffective, redundant, or risky steps, leading to noisy supervision.
The proposed method, SWE-Prime, aims to improve LLM performance by refining the supervision quality beyond simple task success.

stories.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: The paper introduces TTPO (Test-Time Policy Optimization) to address limitations in current post-training methods for LLMs.
Existing methods like RL and OPSD require ground-truth labels, which prevents effective test-time training (TTT).
TTPO proposes using majority-vote pseudo-labels as an alternative to ground truth, while analyzing the fragility and asymmetry of this approach.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitation of current LLM-based code review systems, which treat the process as a single, static decision.
It introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark code review in a dynamic, multi-round, and interactive manner, reflecting real-world development practices.
The research aims to improve the accuracy and realism of automated code review by capturing the iterative problem-solving inherent in human review.

stories.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
stories.author: Dongyan Zhao
bullet_points: The research addresses a key limitation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for LLMs: the collapse of policy entropy.
Entropy collapse in RLVR leads to narrowed reasoning coverage and reduced performance (degraded pass@$k$ for large $k$).
The proposed solution introduces cross-model non-parametric perturbation to maintain generative diversity during RLVR training.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge beyond simple content detection.
The study employs linear probes trained on open-weight models to test for the geometric organization of specific Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
It aims to determine if LLMs can distinguish between different moral foundations (e.g., care/harm vs. fair/cheat) and map their relationships.

stories.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction
stories.author: Guanhua Chen
bullet_points: Clinical language models often fail in real-world deployment due to reliance on note-specific artifacts (templates, boilerplate) rather than true patient state.
The paper introduces CAST (Concept-guided Artifact Suppression Tuning), an SAE-based framework designed to make clinical text classification models auditable.
CAST utilizes Sparse Autoencoders to extract sparse, human-auditable features from Transformer activations, allowing for targeted fine-tuning.

stories.title: RISC-V is now officially supported by CPython
stories.author: lumpa
bullet_points: CPython, the standard Python implementation, now officially supports RISC-V.
This integration is a significant step for bringing RISC-V into mainstream software ecosystems.
It lowers the barrier for developing and running Python applications on RISC-V hardware.

stories.title: What 100% Test Coverage Missed: State Across Google ADK A2A Boundaries
stories.author: arjunganesh
bullet_points: The article discusses a critical failure where a system passed all in-process tests but lost state upon deployment across A2A (Agent-to-Agent) boundaries.
This highlights a common pitfall in software testing: 100% test coverage does not guarantee correctness across distributed boundaries.
The post provides details on the specific boundary issue, the necessary fix, and commentary from Google regarding the problem.

stories.title: Qwen3.8-27B vs Muse Glimmer 30B: Which Permissive Open-Weight Model Fits Your Local GPU?
stories.author: roberts_jakuko_fbc04cb38
bullet_points: Compares two specific open-weight LLMs: Qwen3.8-27B and Muse Glimmer 30B.
Focuses on practical deployment concerns, including Apache 2.0 licensing and 24 GB GPU memory requirements.
Benchmarks include video modalities and local agent serving capabilities.
